title: Proportions of the base, capitals, and entablature in the Ionic order

instance.note: The one column for which chapter 5 gives every number directly: eustyle, 25 Roman feet high.

kinds.S: stated — the number is in the sentence
kinds.R: reconstructed — figure lost or text silent; our reading
kinds.V: variant — an alternative the text offers, not built here
kinds.X: outside this plate — concerns the whole temple

bindings.q: let the height of a column be divided, as in the systyle, into nine and a half parts, and let one part be taken for the thickness at the bottom of the shaft
bindings.name: column height

bindings.q: In a column of from twenty feet to thirty feet, let the bottom of the shaft be divided into seven parts, and let the diminished top measure six of these
bindings.name: diminution of the shaft

bindings.q: at the end of the book a figure and calculation will be subjoined
bindings.name: entasis
bindings.note: The curve is our reading: lower third straight, parabolic diminution above. The dashed line is the same shaft without entasis.

bindings.q: their height, including the plinth, may be half the thickness of a column
bindings.name: base, whole height

bindings.q: their projection (called in Greek ekphora) the same
bindings.name: projection of the base
bindings.f: ½ D in all = ¼ D each side
bindings.note: Read together with the next sentence, which fixes the breadth at 1½ D.

bindings.q: in both length and breadth it will be one and one half thicknesses of a column
bindings.name: plinth, breadth

bindings.q: the upper part shall be one third part of the thickness of the column
bindings.name: base above the plinth

bindings.q: the rest left for the plinth
bindings.name: plinth, height

bindings.q: one fourth constitute the upper torus
bindings.name: upper torus

bindings.q: one part composing the lower torus
bindings.name: lower torus

bindings.q: the other, with its fillets, the scotia
bindings.name: scotia with fillets

bindings.q: equal in breadth to the thickness of a column plus three eighths of the thickness
bindings.name: Ionic base, breadth
bindings.note: The Ionic base is the alternative to the Attic base drawn here.

bindings.q: be divided into seven parts
bindings.name: Ionic base, division

bindings.q: Three of these parts constitute the torus at the top
bindings.name: Ionic base, torus

bindings.q: The astragals must be one eighth of the trochilus
bindings.name: Ionic base, astragals

bindings.q: The projection of the base will be three sixteenths of the thickness of a column
bindings.name: Ionic base, projection

bindings.q: perpendicular to their own centre
bindings.name: axis of the column

bindings.q: their inner sides, which face toward the cella wall, are perpendicular
bindings.name: corner and flank columns

bindings.q: the abacus is in length and breadth equivalent to the thickness of the shaft at its bottom plus one eighteenth thereof
bindings.name: abacus, breadth

bindings.q: the height of the capital, including the volutes, one half of that amount
bindings.name: capital, whole height

bindings.q: recede from the edge of the abacus inwards by one and a half eighteenths of that same amount
bindings.name: volute face, set in from the abacus

bindings.q: the height of the capital is to be divided into nine and a half parts
bindings.name: the part

bindings.q: lines called "catheti" are to be let fall
bindings.name: catheti
bindings.f: plumb lines from the abacus edge

bindings.q: let one and a half be reserved for the height of the abacus
bindings.name: abacus, height

bindings.q: let the other eight be used for the volutes
bindings.name: volutes, height

bindings.q: at a distance of one and a half parts toward the inside from the line previously let fall
bindings.name: cathetus of the eye

bindings.q: leave four and a half parts under the abacus
bindings.name: eye, below the abacus

bindings.q: the remaining three and a half
bindings.name: eye, above the volute's foot

bindings.q: describe a circle with a diameter equal to one of the eight parts
bindings.name: eye of the volute

bindings.q: let the size of each be successively less, by half the diameter of the eye
bindings.name: quadrants of the spiral
bindings.note: Eight quadrants, two full turns, from under the abacus down to the eye.

bindings.q: three parts are below the level of the astragal at the top of the shaft
bindings.name: volute, hanging below the astragal

bindings.q: the rest, omitting the abacus and the channel, belongs to its echinus
bindings.name: echinus
bindings.note: The channel is 2 parts because the spiral's first turn starts 4½ parts above the eye and its second 2½.

bindings.q: The projection of the echinus beyond the fillet of the abacus should be equal to the size of the eye
bindings.name: echinus, projection

bindings.q: place one leg of a pair of compasses in the centre of the capital and open out the other to the edge of the echinus
bindings.name: bands of the cushions

bindings.q: The axes of the volutes should not be thicker than the size of the eye
bindings.name: axes of the volutes

bindings.q: channelled out to a depth which is one twelfth of their height
bindings.name: volute channel, depth

bindings.q: columns twenty-five feet high and less
bindings.name: this column

bindings.q: plus one ninth part thereof
bindings.name: abacus of higher columns

bindings.q: at the end of the book a figure will be subjoined and a calculation showing how they may be described so that their spirals may be true to the compass
bindings.name: the lost figure of the volute
bindings.note: Our reconstruction: four compass centres on a square of ½ part inside the eye. It satisfies every number of §6.

bindings.q: not exactly level on the columns, however, but with the same measured adjustment
bindings.name: capitals follow the stylobate curve

bindings.q: let the height of the architrave be equal to half the thickness of a column at the bottom
bindings.name: architrave, columns 12–15 ft

bindings.q: let the height of a column be measured off into thirteen parts
bindings.name: architrave, columns 15–20 ft

bindings.q: If they are from twenty to twenty-five feet, let this height be divided into twelve and one half parts, and let one of them form the height of the architrave
bindings.name: architrave, height

bindings.q: let it be divided into twelve parts
bindings.name: architrave, columns 25–30 ft

bindings.q: If they are higher, the heights of the architraves are to be worked out proportionately in the same manner
bindings.name: architrave, higher columns

bindings.q: the higher that the eye has to climb, the less easily can it make its way through the thicker and thicker mass of air
bindings.name: why the architrave grows with the column
bindings.f: the eye loses strength with height

bindings.q: there must always be a corresponding increase in the symmetrical proportions of the members
bindings.name: why the proportions increase
bindings.f: so the parts seem in due proportion

bindings.q: equivalent to the thickness of the top of the column just under the capital
bindings.name: architrave, depth below

bindings.q: on its uppermost side equivalent to the foot of the shaft
bindings.name: architrave, depth above

bindings.q: The cymatium of the architrave should be one seventh of the height of the whole architrave
bindings.name: cymatium of the architrave

bindings.q: its projection the same
bindings.name: cymatium, projection

bindings.q: three of these will form the lowest fascia, four, the next, and five, the highest fascia
bindings.name: the three fasciae

bindings.q: one fourth less high than the architrave
bindings.name: frieze

bindings.q: it is one fourth higher than the architrave
bindings.name: frieze with reliefs

bindings.q: Its cymatium is one seventh of the whole height of the frieze
bindings.name: cymatium of the frieze

bindings.q: the projection of the cymatium is the same as its height
bindings.name: frieze cymatium, projection

bindings.q: made of the same height as the middle fascia of the architrave
bindings.name: dentils, height

bindings.q: with a projection equal to their height
bindings.name: dentils, projection

bindings.q: the face of each dentil is half as wide as its height
bindings.name: dentil, face

bindings.q: the cavity of each intersection two thirds of this face in width
bindings.name: dentil, interval

bindings.q: The cymatium here is one sixth of the whole height of this part
bindings.name: cymatium of the dentils

bindings.q: The corona with its cymatium, but not including the sima, has the height of the middle fascia of the architrave
bindings.name: corona

bindings.q: the total projection of the corona and dentils should be equal to the height from the frieze to the cymatium at the top of the corona
bindings.name: corona and dentils, projection

bindings.q: all projecting parts have greater beauty when their projection is equal to their height
bindings.name: the rule of projection

bindings.q: measured off into nine parts
bindings.name: tympanum

bindings.q: one eighth higher than the height of the coronae
bindings.name: sima

bindings.q: The acroteria at the corners have the height of the centre of the tympanum
bindings.name: acroteria

bindings.q: inclined to the front a twelfth part of their own height
bindings.name: inclination of the upper members

bindings.q: it makes that part look as if it were leaning back
bindings.name: why the members lean forward

bindings.q: Each column should have twenty-four flutes
bindings.name: flutes

bindings.q: if a carpenter's square be placed in the hollow of a flute and turned, the arm will touch the corners of the fillets on the right and left
bindings.name: section of a flute
bindings.note: A right angle turning on two fixed points traces a half-circle: the square is the proof.

bindings.q: The breadth of the flutes is to be equivalent to the enlargement in the middle of a column, which will be found in the figure
bindings.name: breadth of the flutes
bindings.note: Our reading: fillet = ¼ of the flute.

bindings.q: one head is marked out directly over the axis of each column
bindings.name: lion's head on the axis

bindings.q: so that there shall be one at the middle of every roof-tiling
bindings.name: lion's heads between
bindings.note: The text does not size the tiles; three to a bay is our reading.

bindings.q: Those that are over the columns should have holes bored through them
bindings.name: pierced head
apophyge and fillets of the shaft
bindings.note: Drawn from surviving Ionic work; chapter 5 does not size them.

bindings.name: egg-and-dart of the echinus
bindings.note: Ornament the chapter does not describe.
